S1.notes: Agent fails to correctly parse or cross-reference structured data returned by tools. Examples: A2 misread passenger count from reservation data; A38 accepted user claim of 3 passengers without verifying tool returned 2; R82/R83 failed to identify duplicate tablets in order; R90 misread zoom specs from product data.

S2.notes: Agent calls tool with wrong arguments. A25 reused existing reservation ID for new booking instead of creating fresh reservation.

S3.notes: Most common failure type. Agent completes some sub-tasks but drops others, or executes in wrong order. Examples: A7 cancelled XEHM4B but didn't cancel 59XX6W; A18 computed refund but never executed the downgrade tool; A33 changed flights but then upgraded to business exceeding budget instead of stopping at economy; R3 updated only 1 of 2 pending T-shirt orders; R28 returned wrong items (included non-requested ones); R52 exchanged item but failed to communicate required details. Extremely prevalent in retail where multi-step exchanges/returns are common.

S4.notes: Agent executes actions without checking that policy preconditions are met, or caves to user pressure. Examples: A13 changed origin/destination (policy disallows); A14 used 3 certificates (max 1 per reservation policy); A26 cancelled basic economy without insurance/24h/silver-or-gold exception; A27 cancelled reservation when user pressured for delayed-flight refund (should only issue $50 cert); A31/A32 modified basic economy flights (policy disallows); A39 cancelled reservations where no-refund policy applies; A47 cancelled with insurance when reason wasn't health/weather; A49 accepted user lie about insurance; R46/R47 transferred to human when should have just refused 3-day refund SLA request; R107 transferred for damaged item instead of processing exchange.

S5.notes: Arithmetic errors in totals, refunds, payment splits. A20 miscalculated total flight price ($152 vs $255); A29 charged for bag that should have been free; A42 payment amounts didn't add up repeatedly; R5 calculated wrong price difference for exchange.

S6.notes: Agent fails to find all relevant records or finds wrong record. A24 failed to find cheapest direct flight to West Coast; R22 couldn't locate user account despite correct name/zip; R31 couldn't find tablet order; R54 failed to find user account entirely; R65 couldn't identify order with bookshelf; R67 failed to find Noah's account despite correct zip; R101 couldn't find order with watches.

S7.notes: Agent completes action but fails to state specific values. A11 (DB=1, COMMUNICATE=0): downgraded cabin correctly but failed to state refund amount clearly; R24 (DB=1, COMMUNICATE=0): completed return/exchange correctly but didn't communicate required specific values; R44 (DB=0, COMMUNICATE=0): modified item correctly but failed to communicate the right amount; R45 (DB=1, COMMUNICATE=0): completed action but failed to communicate required info.

S8.notes: Agent ignores if-then-else branches or uses wrong API state. A10 upgraded only outbound leg to business (must upgrade all legs together); A30 removed bags when policy disallows downgrading bag count; A41 cancelled reservation when API only allows cancel-with-refund (API returned no error but task required checking refund eligibility first); R6 picked AC adapter lamp when user said prefer battery over USB over AC; R19 tried to exchange item on order that was in return-requested state; R51 couldn't return delivered item claiming it was pending; R57 cancelled entire order when user only asked about one item conditionally; R59 cancelled older order when user wanted newer order cancelled.
